'Brain lies' had the best skip rate (51.7), and that also used a list. The topic is new and interactive: viewers can check their own wrist tendon and ear muscles. topic: Vestigial body parts: palmaris longus, ear muscles, plica semilunaris, tailbone, wisdom teeth
hook: 5 body parts evolution forgot to delete

slides.title: The wrist tendon
slides.body: Touch thumb to pinky and flex your wrist. No raised tendon? In many studies, about 15% of people lack it.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical model of a forearm and wrist with one glowing tendon highlighted, soft studio lighting, clean dark background

slides.title: Ear muscles
slides.body: Our ancestors swiveled their ears. A 2020 study found yours still twitch toward sounds, just too weakly to move.
slides.image_prompt: Plaster anatomical model of a human ear with tiny muscles highlighted in red, sound waves drawn as glowing rings around it

slides.title: A third eyelid
slides.body: The small pink fold in your eye's inner corner is thought to be a leftover of the third eyelid birds still use.
slides.image_prompt: Close-up of an owl eye with a translucent third eyelid half closed, dramatic macro lighting

slides.title: Your tailbone
slides.body: Every human embryo has a tail for a few weeks. It shrinks before birth, leaving the coccyx at your spine's base.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical skeleton model of a lower spine with the tailbone glowing softly, museum lighting, dark background

slides.title: Wisdom teeth
slides.body: Our jaws shrank, so they often don't fit. About 22% of people are missing at least one entirely.
slides.image_prompt: Dental model of a human jaw with crowded wisdom teeth highlighted in gold, clean clinical lighting

cta: Part 2 tomorrow. Follow to catch it
caption:
Your body still carries parts from ancestors who lived very differently. Some people have a wrist tendon that others simply don't. And the muscles behind your ears still fire when a sound grabs your attention, even though they can no longer move your ears.

Evolution doesn't delete what isn't harmful. It just lets it fade. Part 2 drops tomorrow, so follow @you.didnot.know for one fact a day your body won't believe.

Try the thumb-to-pinky test right now: do you have the tendon? 👇
